calls.title: Demos
calls.description: The aim with Demos is to facilitate networks and meetings between civil society organisations in the Nordics. A strong and dynamic civil society is a cornerstone of Nordic democracy. The funding programme promotes the ability of stakeholders in Nordic civil society to work together, to influence, and to strengthen their voice. The partnerships will help the Nordic Region on its way to becoming the most sustainable and integrated region in the world by 2030.
calls.requirements:
Please note that only civil society organisations can apply for funding.

Funding can be applied for by non-profit civil society organisations in all areas of society . These organisations include associations, foundations, charities, citizens organisations, interest groups, labour market organisations, religious communities, social enterprises, and NGOs. Demos funds projects with participation from at least three (3) different Nordic countries. Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Åland are considered as separate countries in this context. To be eligible, the applicant organisation must be established and registered in the Nordic Region. Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Åland are considered as Nordic countries in this context. Although the project may cover additional partners who do not operate in the Nordic Region, at least three Nordic countries must be represented. The partner is considered to represent the country or area in which the organisation is registered. The organisation and partners must have a democratic structure and operations. The organisation and partners must not pursue making a profit. The organisation must not owe taxes or fees to the state and must not have applied for bankruptcy or be in liquidation. Please note that individuals cannot apply for funding.

calls.title: New Norwegian fiction for adults – automatic acquisition scheme
calls.description: The scheme shall contribute to new Norwegian fiction for adults being created, published, distributed and read.
calls.requirements: Publishers and other publishers with a Norwegian organisation number can submit books to this scheme. It is not possible to submit books to both the automatic and the selective acquisition scheme for new Norwegian fiction for the same target group within the same publication year. It is important that you as the publisher have entered into an agreement with the author and any other rights holders (such as illustrators or translators) before you apply. The Arts Council of Norway can decide that a publisher is not allowed to submit books for a period if they have not complied with the conditions for the scheme previously. For example, this may be because the publisher has not repaid money by the stated deadlines. Remember that an author can usually only have one book for adults and one book for children and young people submitted to the acquisition schemes for fiction each calendar year. This is called the “one-book rule.” The one-book rule applies to this scheme and the selective acquisition scheme for fiction for adults together. This means that the author cannot have more than one book submitted to the acquisition schemes for fiction for adults in the same year. You can apply for an exemption from the one-book rule on behalf of the author. You must do this before the first book is published. The application must be justified. The book must be new Norwegian fiction for adults. By fiction we mean novels, short stories, short prose, poetry, drama and picture books. Under this scheme, we classify drama in metrical form as poetry. We also classify books with mainly fact-based and professional content as fiction if the books have a sufficiently literary character. The book must either be written in Norwegian (Bokmål, Nynorsk or dialect) or translated into Norwegian from Sámi or a national minority language or translated into Norwegian from another language if it is an original work that has not been published previously, or a translation of poetry into Norwegian. By new we mean that the book is published as an original work in the same year that you apply. Translations of poetry into Norwegian are considered new literary works. Collections of poems and short stories are considered new if less than half of the content has been printed previously. In any case, the collection must be assessed as a unified literary work. If the author of the book is deceased, you can apply for up to five years after the author passed away. If the book is translated from Sámi or a national minority language, the original work cannot be more than five years old when you apply.

calls.title: State Artist Grant
calls.description: The State Artist Grant shall contribute to the state art policy by facilitating that individual artists, through direct grants from the state, can contribute to a diverse and innovative art life of high quality. The grants shall give artists the opportunity to develop their artistic activity and have artistic activity as their main occupation.
calls.requirements:
The grant is primarily for artists who live and work in Norway
Artists who primarily live and work in Norway may receive a grant from the State Artist Grant. Exceptions may be made to the requirement that you must primarily live and work in Norway if your artistic activity has an impact on the arts and cultural life in Norway. Your artistic practice may have an impact on Norwegian arts and cultural life if, through your artistic work, you have particular connections to Norway or Norwegian arts and cultural life. The artistic practice must be significant for the arts field.

The grant is for professionally active artists
You must be a professionally active artist to receive the grant. You are considered a professionally active artist if the relevant art field is your professional occupation. What constitutes having art as a professional occupation may vary between art fields, but involves work creating or performing art for professional purposes. The term “professional” also indicates that the artist has competence, either based on education or on documented practice. Normally, professional professional activity will involve income from the work.

Restrictions related to education and employment
You cannot receive the grant if you are undertaking education equivalent to more than 15 ECTS credits per semester.
You cannot receive the grant if you have employment relationships totaling more than 50 percent of a full-time position during the calendar year in which you receive the grant. This applies to work grants, work grants for newly established artists, grants for established artists, and grants for senior artists.
You may be employed in a position exceeding 50 percent and receive miscellaneous grants and start-up grants for young artists.
Being employed in a “position” means all types of employment relationships, including temporary and short-term positions. Freelance work or other short-term commission agreements do not count as a “position.” That the position may not exceed 50 percent in total for the calendar year means that the average percentage of the position for the entire year in which you receive the grant may not be over 50 percent. If you have a position exceeding 50 percent at the start of the year, the position must be reduced so that the total workload in employment relationships for the entire calendar year does not exceed 50 percent. The purpose of the rule is that you should have at least 50 percent free working time in the year you receive the grant, so that you can use the grant to develop your artistic practice.

Combination of different grants
You cannot receive more than one grant of the type work grant, work grant for newly established artists, grant for established artists, or grant for senior artists at the same time. If you receive one of these grants, you may still receive a miscellaneous grant or a start-up grant for young artists in addition. Recipients of state grants cannot receive a grant from the State Artist Grant.

calls.title: 1.1.1 Creation and staging of a stage work – theatre
calls.description: Subprogramme 1.1 – Theatre is focused on supporting drama theatre, musical-dramatic theatre, puppet theatre, theatre for children and youth, and other alternative forms of theatre, with the aim of maintaining the continuity of theatre culture, supporting new artistic forms and non-commercial activities.
calls.requirements: Support is intended for theatre collectives defined in the description of programme 1.1, which are established on the Slovak art scene and active on it. Support in this subprogramme is intended exclusively for: the creation and staging of a stage work that will be publicly presented in the 2026/2027 season; a condition for the granting of support is also repeated performances in the following 2027/2028 season. Support is not intended for: separate repeated performances of a stage work that has already been staged, writing a theatre work, creation without being linked to a specific stage performance of the work. The substantive output must in the future be staged as a stage work, which the applicant confirms by an acceptance letter from the institution in which the work will be realised, rehearsal of an individual performance, ordinary operating expenses of the theatre, stage works presented exclusively online. Within the subprogramme, the applicant may submit a maximum of three applications for the allocation of financial resources. In the event that the applicant submits more than three applications, the fund will consider only the first three delivered applications, or the first three applications with a lower serial number, as complete, and the others will be excluded. An application for support may be submitted only by an applicant who has, by the deadline of the call for applications, completed the implementation of their project, if they were supported in previous years of the FPU support activity. A project is considered completed if the recipient submitted the substantive evaluation of the project to the fund after the expiration of the entire period for which the support was granted. If multiple entities participate in the implementation of the project, the application is submitted exclusively by the entity that initiated the work or is responsible for its implementation. Only one entity may apply for support for the implementation of the identical work. In the event that more than one application is submitted for the identical work (the content is decisive, not the title), the fund will consider only the first delivered application, or the application with a lower serial number, as complete, and the others will be excluded.

calls.title: Craft and design projects in Denmark and abroad
calls.description: Funding for projects for and with Danish craft and design in Denmark and abroad.
calls.requirements: The Committee for Craft and Design Project Funding funds artists, designers, curators, authors, promoters, museums, galleries and others with an interest in developing and promoting craft and design in Denmark and Danish craft and design abroad in the form of projects. You can read more about how the committee defines a project under the "What is the purpose of the programme" section of this page. Examples of projects that the committee may fund include: Exhibitions and dissemination projects as well as exhibition series and annual programmes that involve works by contemporary artists and designers in Denmark and/or abroad. Residencies and exchange/work stays Production of works Projects that show aesthetic potential and a thorough understanding of a craft, materials and sensuousness Projects that are centered on concrete design solutions to specific problems or projects that are more immaterial or critical in nature. Presentations and all types of dissemination (verbal, written, visual, digital and printed) of the works of contemporary Danish artists and designers to a relevant audience, this includes travel funding and residencies in connection with specific exhibitions and tasks Funding for establishing a business and international cooperation on the production of new types of Danish craft and design products that contribute to demonstrating the special identity and profile of the craft or design Editorial content production for different media: reviews, articles, dissemination of academic research projects etc. Find out more about how to apply if your project combines different art forms. You cannot receive funding for: Activities completed before the application deadline Courses of study/training courses Projects that the committee have previously supported Capital investments and operating expenses Expenses from previous calendar years. That is, only expenses from either the same or upcoming calendar year can be entered into the budget

calls.title: Nordic translations
calls.description: Funding for Nordic publishers to cover fees for translators, translating a work from Danish into another Nordic language.
calls.requirements: Who may apply? Nordic publishers wishing to publish a work translated from Danish into another Nordic language. Non-Nordic publishers: please apply to the fund ‘Literary production and translation’. Applications should be made in the Nordic country in which the work was originally published. For the translation of works from Danish, you should therefore submit your application to the Danish Arts Foundation's Committee for Literary Project Funding. Before submitting the application, the applicant must have acquired the copyrights for the literary work and signed a contract with a translator. Projects may not be finished before the expiry of the application deadline. You can apply for: Fiction for adults, children and young adults General cultural literature and non-fiction Essays Comics and graphic novels You cannot receive funding for: translation of works within the areas of research, education, regional and local history, handbooks, hobby books, self-help books, and catalogues translation of your own works and text revision Furthermore, funding is typically not awarded to Danish publishers for publication of Danish works in translation.
